titleStmt.title: Jekyll and Hyde Research Encoding — Demonstration Sample

publicationStmt.p: Created as a partial demonstration encoding for computational-literary research.

sourceDesc.p: Structural demonstration based on the public-domain text; not a complete diplomatic edition.

div.head: STORY OF THE DOOR
div.p: Mr. Utterson walks with Mr. Enfield and hears the first account of Mr. Hyde.

div.head: INCIDENT OF THE LETTER
div.p: Utterson examines a letter associated with Dr. Jekyll and Hyde.

div.head: Hyde letter — demonstration encoding
div.p: An embedded document whose material hand becomes an object of reading by Utterson and Mr. Guest.
div.note: This is metadata-oriented demonstration text, not a diplomatic transcription.
This sample encodes structure, entities, documents, and relations rather than reproducing a full edition.

div.head: THE LAST NIGHT
div.p: This demonstration layer records a material transfer of documents to Utterson.

div.head: Document packet — demonstration encoding
div.p: A metadata-oriented document object used to represent the packet referenced by the research annotation and evidence-link layers.
div.note: No Stevenson wording is reproduced here; this object exists for structural and referential modeling.

div.head: HENRY JEKYLL'S FULL STATEMENT OF THE CASE
div.p: This demonstration layer records the confessional document addressed through the narrative's readerly and documentary structure.

div.head: Jekyll confession — demonstration encoding
div.p: A metadata-oriented document object used to represent the confession referenced by the research annotation and evidence-link layers.
div.note: No Stevenson wording is reproduced here; this object exists for structural and referential modeling.
